title: Islam: five prayers
hookLine: Muslims pray five times a day, facing Mecca

cards: Pings, buzzes, banners: a phone's interruptions pull toward something someone else wants. Salat is an interruption of another kind.
Five times, from before dawn to after dark, a Muslim who keeps the prayers stops what they're doing, washes, turns in one direction, and prays toward God.
And because the times follow the sun, as dawn and dusk move across the time zones, a wave of prayer rolls around the planet all day. Today: salat, the five daily prayers.

teach.b: Salat is the second pillar of Islam, after the shahada. The five prayers have names, and they follow the sun. Fajr, before dawn.
Dhuhr, just after midday. Asr, in the afternoon. Maghrib, just after sunset.
Isha, at night. Before praying, Muslims wash in a set way, called wudu: hands, mouth, nose, face, arms, head, ears, feet.
Then they face the qibla, the direction of the Kaaba in Mecca. At first the early Muslims faced Jerusalem, and the Qur'an records the change of direction in its second chapter.
Each prayer is made of cycles of standing, bowing, prostrating with the forehead on the ground, and sitting, reciting the Qur'an in Arabic, beginning with its opening chapter. Why five?
A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari tells of the night journey of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, when fifty daily prayers were first commanded.

On the way back, Moses, the story goes, urged him to return and ask for fewer, and he went back again and again until they were five, with the reward of fifty. The Qur'an gives the purpose in a line to Moses himself.
In Pickthall's 1930 translation, God says, "establish worship for My remembrance."
So the five prayers are, among other things, a way to remember God five times, before the day can make you forget. Practice varies a little.
In Shia practice the five prayers are commonly joined into three sessions, and Sunni Muslims may join them when traveling.
Mosques call people to each one, but the prayer can be made anywhere clean: an office, a park, an airport floor.

how: Muslims pray salat five times a day at set times, after washing with wudu and facing the Kaaba in Mecca, alone or together; on Fridays the midday prayer is held in congregation at the mosque.

games.q: on the night journey, fifty daily prayers are commanded. on the way back, Moses stops the Prophet. what does he urge?
o: go back and ask for fewer.
games.why: in the hadith, Moses urges him to return again and again, until they're five, with the reward of fifty.

practice: Imagine your day with five pauses in it: waking, midday, afternoon, sunset, bedtime. Rehearse them now, one by one, picturing yourself stopping for a single minute at each.
If you pray, that minute can be prayer; if not, a breath, a thank-you, turning your attention toward what matters most.
